planner_self_verification.why: v2 defect 3 was a wrong factual claim about PostgreSQL rendering asserted without probing. Before submitting v3 the planner probed every new SQL claim on the live PostgreSQL 16.14 container rather than reasoning from memory.
results: regexp_count exists (PG15+) and returns 2 for a duplicated JSON key, 1 for a single key.
A duplicate key does collapse at ::jsonb, last value winning: {"name":"x","name":"y"} yields "y". The count check therefore has to inspect the raw text, as the plan specifies.
jsonb_typeof returns number for 7 while ->> coerces the same value to the text 7 — the exact laundering path defect 4 identified; the type gate must run first, as the plan specifies.

Digest binding is well-defined: sha256 over the stored canonical text is 4d88235c... while sha256 over the same document rendered by PostgreSQL ::text is d88776d5... The two genuinely differ, so probe D-25b cannot pass vacuously and the defect-3 premise is confirmed.
Exact key-set comparison via array_agg over jsonb_object_keys detects an extra top-level key.

The duplicate-key regexp has no false positives: a value containing the literal text "domain_label": still counts 1, because JSON escapes the inner quotes; and a key that is a substring of another key (key vs asset_key) counts 1 each, because the opening quote anchors the boundary.
planner_self_verification.correction: The claim recorded earlier — that the duplicate-key regexp "has no false positives" — was true as far as it went and misleading as a soundness claim. The probe set covered a value mimicking a key and a key that is a substring of another key, but NOT a Unicode-escaped key name. The reviewer probed that case and it is a real bypass, re-verified by the planner on PostgreSQL 16.14: for {"asset_key":"bad","\u0061sset_key":"good"}, regexp_count returns 1 while json_each decodes two asset_key entries and JSONB keeps "good" — so the DB verifies "good" while the human-visible canonical text says "bad", defeating the premise that the canonical bytes are the identity. Also re-verified: reordered check-result text is JSONB-equal to the canonical form, byte-different, and digest-self-consistent, so nothing in the specified guard forces actual canonical ordering. Incomplete verification is not verification; the record is corrected rather than left standing.

replan.root_cause_addressed: Every rejected version tried to make a database constraint prove something a database cannot prove: that a text blob is a canonical serialization, that a recorded result was computed, that a declared tool scope matches code behaviour. The new plan stops reaching for forgery resistance against admin write access and records only what the datastore enforces.
what_changed: Identity is the row, not a hash. Because the tables are append-only a row never changes, so a foreign key to catalog_assets.id is already a binding to immutable content. identity_canonical_json, the content_hash CHECK, and the deferrable rebind trigger are deleted outright — with them go the escaped-key, duplicate-key, type-coercion and extra-key evasions.

Vetting results are typed child rows keyed UNIQUE(record, check_name), not a JSONB array with a canonical-text column and a digest. No serialization exists, so none can be non-canonical. Cardinality and outcome derivation are dual deferred triggers, the Slice-37/40 pattern.

Provenance renamed to what it is: checker_output_admin_recorded and reviewer_asserted_admin_recorded. The plan states plainly that the DB cannot see which code produced a payload and that the label is app-stamped.
The AST tool-scope equality check is dropped entirely rather than patched a third time. Declared scope is declared and unverified, and the permission-scoped claim is refused.
The only digest retained, reference intake content_sha256, is labelled registrar-supplied drift-detection metadata and explicitly not authenticity or non-repudiation, per the owner's constraint.
Seven tables, 585 plan lines, versus the superseded five tables and 800+ lines of guard machinery.
replan.deferred_with_owner_entries: Section 7 of the plan lists every dropped capability with a one-line reason. Three are spec-required and get roadmap section 12 OPEN entries with owner=Salim, added by the builder in the same PR: D-8 verified permission scoping (App. C l.3012), D-9 real-provider connector testing (App. C l.3012), D-10 automated blueprint security scanning (App. C l.3010).
replan.v1_reject: v1 REJECT by cacd3b79-15df-4d15-899f-1514426cb9a1: (1) connector identity not frozen — append-only parent rows do not freeze child inserts, so a second tool_scope row could land after listing; (2) section 8 scheduled a false roadmap-exit claim for 61b while D-8/D-9/D-10 remain open; (3) D-10 tracked automated scanning rather than an evidence-backed security-review gate, and section 0.6 overclaimed a performed review.
v2_fixes: OD-13: tool-scope pins (asset_id, asset_kind); catalog_connector_children_complete required at vetting and listing; spec/scope INSERT refused once any vetting record exists; both triggers FOR UPDATE the asset row. Probes D-21a through D-21h.
61b populates the declared catalog and does not close the roadmap Slice 61 exit. Header, 0.7, 6, 7, and 8 now agree.
D-10 is an evidence-backed security-review gate (verified human workflow or scanner). Allowed claim is a reviewer-asserted record labelled blueprint_security_review, not a performed review.
replan.halt_watch: Cleared. Plan approved on the third from-scratch review. Halt rules remain in force for code review: three consecutive code REJECTs halt and report.
replan.v2_reject: v2 REJECT by cacd3b79-15df-4d15-899f-1514426cb9a1: (1) race outcome overspecified — FOR UPDATE serializes but child-first lets both commit (scopes=2, vettings=1), contradicting "cannot both succeed" / "exactly one commits"; record_contract_test must lock before loading children; "children the checker ran against" was unsupported; (2) listing-guard clause 7 had no behavioural test — helper unit test plus source-text mention is not a guard firing.
v3_fixes: Both linearizations specified and probed (D-21h): vetting-first freezes the later child; child-first both commit and the extra child is in the frozen pre-vetting set. Forbidden outcome is a child committing after a vetting row.

record_contract_test locks the asset before loading children and running the checker (D-21i), so checker input equals the frozen set. Claim language is "children present when the vetting row was inserted" except on that repository path.

D-22 clause 7: admin disables freeze and vetting guards only, inserts incomplete connector plus passing-shaped vetting row, re-enables, listing guard stays enabled throughout, listing INSERT refused with listing_connector_children_required. No replica-role.
replan.verbatim: APPROVE. Both PostgreSQL lock linearizations are now correctly specified; only post-vetting child insertion is forbidden. record_contract_test locks before loading children and running checks. Clause 7 now behaviorally exercises the listing guard. PostgreSQL confirmed disabling one named trigger leaves the listing trigger tgenabled=O; it fired and prevented insertion. No stale race or performed-review/61b-exit overclaims remain outside historical quotations. Frozen hashes match the tree.
